selections.sense: despite a circumstance that might be expected to prevent the result
selections.levelRationale: Nominal concession lets a speaker acknowledge an obstacle while maintaining the conclusion; checked pragmatics1.2.1 B2 supports this contrast.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Reuse the exact sense of B1-F-101; A1-F251 pero is the earlier generic contrast, while B1-F098 así que gives an earlier ordinary consequence.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless usage notes state otherwise; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: A pesar de+noun/infinitive; a pesar de que+clause needs separate mood scoping.
selections.pronunciationNotes: a pe-SAR de; final r; de unstressed.
uncertainties: Same meaning as A2-D187/B1-D025/B1-F101; retain baseline B2, with final ADP versus a pesar de que clause granularity left to F/D.

selections.sense: nevertheless, marking an unexpected contrast with a preceding statement
selections.levelRationale: The same unexpected-contrast connector already supports connected B1 explanations, and checked pragmatics1.2.1 explicitly lists it in B1.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Reuse the exact sense of B1-F-102; A1-F251 pero is the earlier generic contrast, while B1-F098 así que gives an earlier ordinary consequence.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless usage notes state otherwise; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Invariable discourse adverb; punctuation separates units according to syntax, not obligatory identical pauses.
selections.pronunciationNotes: sin em-BAR-go; g hard before o.
uncertainties: Propose B1 in agreement with B1-D026, against B1-F102 and A2-D188 retaining the B2 baseline; no runtime change.

selections.sense: therefore, presenting a conclusion from preceding information
selections.levelRationale: Drawing an explicit consequence is already a B1 discourse function; pragmatics1.2.1 places this connector in that column.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Reuse the exact sense of B1-F-103; A1-F251 pero is the earlier generic contrast, while B1-F098 así que gives an earlier ordinary consequence.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless usage notes state otherwise; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Fixed phrase; lo not gender-agreeing object; sentence adverb.
selections.pronunciationNotes: por lo TAN-to; function-word linking.
uncertainties: Propose B1 with B1-D027 against B1-F103/A2-D189 and the current B2 baseline; introductory-level adjudication remains open.

selections.sense: by contrast, presenting a different property or situation
selections.levelRationale: A paired comparison of distinct situations is a useful B2 contrast resource in checked pragmatics1.2.1; not merely unexpected-result concession.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Reuse the exact sense of B1-F-104; A1-F251 pero is the earlier generic contrast, while B1-F098 así que gives an earlier ordinary consequence.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless usage notes state otherwise; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Invariable; contrast of paired topics/situations; not cash change cambio.
selections.pronunciationNotes: en CAM-bio; io diphthong.
uncertainties: Same baseline meaning in A2-D190/B1-D028/B1-F104. B2 retained as a proposal, not proof no learner can use it earlier.

selections.sense: infer that a proposition is probably true
selections.levelRationale: Infer a likely explanation from available clues rather than describe a duty; grammar12.1 explicitly supplies this B2 periphrase.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F021 deber obligation and A1-F226 poder possibility do not express this particular inference; keep inferred necessity separate from a duty.
selections.register: neutral; pragmatic force or possible offense noted where relevant
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless usage notes state otherwise; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Deber (de)+infinitive; regular deberé/debería, not contracted debr-. De is usual for supposition but not obligatory; do not teach an absolute de-versus-no-de rule.
selections.pronunciationNotes: de-BER de; unstressed de and infinitive grouped.
uncertainties: Same meaning as B1-F293 later disposition. De is a useful teaching contrast, not an exclusive grammatical diagnostic: current RAE admits supposition with deber and occasional obligation with deber de.

selections.sense: close to a stated amount, without claiming exactness
selections.levelRationale: Numerical estimation is already covered by B1-F037, so a longer B2 estimate does not create a new introductory meaning.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F123 más o menos expresses a rough estimate; the same closer-to-written approximation adverb is already selected in B1-F037.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic unless usage notes state otherwise; es-ES audio
selections.formNotes: Invariable -mente adverb; modifies quantity/time; not 'at least'.
selections.pronunciationNotes: a-pro-xi-MA-da-MEN-te has the adjective-derived and -mente stress sites; x usually /ks/, with ordinary connected-speech variation.
uncertainties: The approved B2 illustrative seed is inherited B1 here; exact scenario use versus introduction must be globally reconciled.

selections.sense: situation in which too little of something is available
selections.levelRationale: The ordinary shortage concept is already a B1-S196 proposal; retain that earlier introduction rather than invent a B2 sense solely for discussing supply in more depth.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F119 poco expresses quantity and A2-F040 suficiente adequacy; B1-S196 already names this shortage state.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine la escasez; plural escaseces; escasez de a resource, not scarcity of physical size.
selections.pronunciationNotes: es-ca-SEZ; final stress, z /θ/ or /s/ by variety; plural es-ca-SE-ces.
uncertainties: B1-S196 B1 conflicts with the approved B2-F seed. No literal escasez found in the checked B1/B2 or C1/C2 general-notion pages; original B1 proposal is not an official lexical placement.

selections.sense: remove an element or option so that it no longer forms part of a set
selections.levelRationale: Practical reasoning needs deliberate exclusion of an option rather than only destroying an object; this general removal meaning is proposed for B2.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-W111 deleting a digital item may be a contextual subtype of this operation; B1-F070 destruir causes destruction, which exclusion need not do.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Transitive eliminar algo/de una lista; regular -ar; competition elimination is a separate possible subtype, not selected through this gloss.
selections.pronunciationNotes: e-li-mi-NAR; retain all unstressed vowels; final r.
uncertainties: A2-W111 earlier digital removal may justify an A2 general parent; this B2 generalization must be adjudicated, not counted automatically as a separate meaning.

selections.sense: cause an event or reaction, often one that is unwanted
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes bringing a result about from merely reporting that it occurred, useful when explaining causal chains.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-S192 causar already expresses bringing about an event/result; B1-F001 ocurrir and002 suceder only report occurrence. Provocar is a causative lexical/valency choice, not the first causation meaning.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Provocar algo/que+subjunctive; provoco but provoque preserves /k/; deliberate provocation of a person is outside this selected result sense.
selections.pronunciationNotes: pro-vo-CAR; /k/ in ca and que; voiced b/v have no phonemic contrast.
uncertainties: Compare exact B1-S192 causar: proposed B2 introduction of provocar needs synonym/register judgment, not a first-causation rationale.

selections.sense: put a rule, arrangement or system into operation
selections.levelRationale: Allows a speaker to describe creating operative conditions rather than only physically making something.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F067 crear is broader creation; B1-W187 acordar reaches a shared decision but does not necessarily implement an operative system.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Establecer algo; establezco/establezca; established participle establecido, no adjective duplicate here.
selections.pronunciationNotes: es-ta-ble-CER; /θ/ or /s/ in ce, /sk/ or /θk/ sequence in establezco depending variety.
uncertainties: Overlap with creating or agreeing procedures is a granularity decision; selecting this institutional establishment sense is not a claim every harder crear context needs B2.

selections.sense: state of being in a place or taking part where one is expected
selections.levelRationale: Names attendance/presence as a condition to discuss requirements and participation instead of merely locating a person.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-W072 asistir already means attend an event; the abstract state noun is distinct but paired with that earlier verb.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine la presencia; presencia de alguien, con/en presencia de; physical appearance or commanding bearing not selected.
selections.pronunciationNotes: pre-SEN-cia; final cia diphthong, c /θ/ or /s/.

selections.sense: state of not being where someone or something is expected
selections.levelRationale: Provides the contrasting condition for explaining gaps or nonattendance without assuming permission or a cause.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-T104/B1-H117 faltar already mark a missing expected item; ausencia packages the state, not a new missing-item verb.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine la ausencia; ausencia de; plural ausencias for separate missed occasions.
selections.pronunciationNotes: au-SEN-cia; au and ia are usual diphthongs; c follows regional /θ/ or /s/.

selections.sense: remain in excess of what is needed or used
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes leftover excess from merely having a large quantity; useful in resource allocation and explaining waste.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F118 mucho expresses amount; A2-F038 demasiado expresses excess degree, but neither directly predicates that usable items remain beyond need.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: The surplus item is subject: sobra/sobran; a person may be indirect experiencer; exclude social rejection reading of sobrar someone.
selections.pronunciationNotes: so-BRAR; br cluster and final r.
uncertainties: Household leftovers may support an earlier introduction; no exact sobrar row appears in the inspected saved A1/A2/B1 index.

selections.sense: have a person or resource available to rely on for an intended action
selections.levelRationale: Explaining feasibility requires available support as a condition, distinct from counting units or narrating a story.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F124 contar enumerates quantities and B1-F286 contar recounts a story; neither conveys dependable availability.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Contar con+noun or con que+clause; cuento/cuente; do not omit con; reliance and resource availability may merit later subdivision.
selections.pronunciationNotes: con-TAR con; repeated con syllables remain intelligible; cuento /kwe/.
uncertainties: Availability and personal reliance are provisionally one bounded support sense; final parent granularity must be adjudicated.

selections.sense: available means used to meet a need or carry out an activity
selections.levelRationale: Reuse the B1-S198 earlier proposal for ordinary available means; discussing a more complicated plan does not change this baseline meaning.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1 concrete tools and money can serve as resources; B1-S198 already selects the general means concept, whereas B1-W022 retains B2.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Masculine recurso; usually count plural recursos; recurso para/de context; legal appeal is not this sense.
selections.pronunciationNotes: re-CUR-so; initial r trill and medial tap.
uncertainties: B1-S198 B1 conflicts with B1-W022 and A1-S156/A2-S183 B2 retention. Same baseline identity, pending global introduction decision.

selections.sense: feature used to describe or distinguish a person, object or group
selections.levelRationale: Supports explicit criteria for comparing options rather than a list of disconnected adjectives.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F078 cualidad describes a quality; A2-D080 tipo names the class, not the distinguishing feature that defines it.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine noun característica; plural características; adjective característico requires separate POS/meaning selection if needed.
selections.pronunciationNotes: ca-rac-te-RÍS-ti-ca; written accent, ct/kt/ sequence across syllables.

selections.sense: group established by a chosen classification criterion
selections.levelRationale: A labelled classification group allows organized comparisons and records rather than merely naming an item.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-D080 tipo and A2-D081 clase already express kinds; categoría is a more explicit classification label, not a new claim that grouping starts at B2.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine categoría; categorías; pertenecer a una categoría; exclude high social standing use.
selections.pronunciationNotes: ca-te-go-RÍ-a; í-a hiatus.
uncertainties: Synonym/register economy with tipo/clase and B1-W075 clasificar requires review; B2 is proposed lexical introduction, not a different grouping operation.

selections.sense: be a member or constituent of a specified group
selections.levelRationale: Explains the relation between an item and a class or organization without confusing membership with location.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-D080 tipo and B1-W075 clasificar name the group and sorting action, not the relation of belonging to it.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Pertenecer a; pertenezco/pertenezca; ownership by a person may share the relation but is not selected as a separate sense here.
selections.pronunciationNotes: per-te-ne-CER; pertenezco /θk/ or /sk/; final r.
uncertainties: Group membership versus possession and the construction formar parte de need a final shared-parent decision.

selections.sense: be constituted by the specified component parts
selections.levelRationale: Allows an explanation of how a whole is built from parts, rather than just naming materials.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-F145 de marks material and B1-F121 tercio a share; neither supplies the whole-to-components predicate.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Pronominal componerse de; compone, compuesto; component agreement with the whole as subject; composing art is separate.
selections.pronunciationNotes: com-po-NER-se de; compuesto /pwes/; se and de unstressed.

selections.sense: have specified actions or features as the defining content of something
selections.levelRationale: Clarifies what a task or procedure actually involves, beyond listing its physical ingredients.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Componerse de in this batch describes constituent parts; A1-F225 hacer says perform a task without defining its content.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Consistir en+noun/infinitive, or en que+clause; regular -ir; do not substitute de mechanically.
selections.pronunciationNotes: con-sis-TIR en; link final r into the following vowel.

selections.sense: something that occurred or is presented as an established fact
selections.levelRationale: A bounded fact/event noun is needed when separating an observed occurrence from an interpretation.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F001 ocurrir reports occurrence and B1-F005 mientras relates events; hecho as a noun is not an extra form of hacer.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Masculine hecho; hechos; distinguish nominal fact/event from hecho participle and evaluative fixed phrases.
selections.pronunciationNotes: HE-cho; h silent, ch /tʃ/.
uncertainties: Occurrence versus verified-fact construal is provisionally grouped; do not imply that calling something un hecho establishes its truth.

selections.sense: unplanned correspondence or concurrence between otherwise separate circumstances
selections.levelRationale: Explains why two things can coincide without a causal connection or advance arrangement.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F034 al mismo tiempo only states simultaneity; coincidence can involve matching details at different times.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine coincidencia; coincidencias; coincidencia entre/de; deliberate agreement is a different sense.
selections.pronunciationNotes: coincidencia stresses DEN; oi may be grouped differently in ordinary speech, so do not mandate initial hiatus; final cia usually a diphthong.

selections.sense: without deliberate intention or advance arrangement
selections.levelRationale: Marks accidental occurrence without presenting it as fortunate; useful when explaining how information or people were encountered.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F011 por suerte evaluates good fortune; an accidental outcome may be favourable or unfavourable.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Invariable prepositional adverbial; no agreement; casualidad noun parent can be adjudicated without automatically authoring both.
selections.pronunciationNotes: por ca-sua-li-DAD; ua diphthong; final d may weaken naturally.
uncertainties: The phrase rather than a separate casualidad noun is selected for bounded accidental-event narration; granularity remains open.

selections.sense: degree or prospect of something being true or happening
selections.levelRationale: Names the strength of a possibility for comparing explanations rather than merely saying possibly.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-F004 probable and B1-F027 probablemente already express likelihood; the noun enables discussion of differing probabilities, not a new certainty claim.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine probabilidad; probabilidad de+noun/infinitive or de que+subjunctive; not a statistical-calculation course.
selections.pronunciationNotes: pro-ba-bi-li-DAD; repeated unstressed syllables and final d.

selections.sense: provisional explanation or assumption considered before confirmation
selections.levelRationale: Allows a speaker to distinguish a working explanation from a demonstrated conclusion.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F237 creer expresses belief; B1-F274 suponer assumes, but does not name a testable or provisional explanation.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine la hipótesis/las hipótesis, number shown by determiner; formular/comprobar una hipótesis.
selections.pronunciationNotes: hi-PÓ-te-sis; h silent, accent on pó; no plural added -es.

selections.sense: confidence that a proposition is true rather than merely possible
selections.levelRationale: Can delimit what is known confidently versus what remains inferred in an explanation.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-F006 seguro expresses certainty as a quality; B1-F082 duda names the opposing uncertainty state.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine certeza; tener certeza de+noun phrase or de que+clause; con certeza; confidence is not necessarily truth.
selections.pronunciationNotes: cer-TE-za; both c/z follow /θ/ or /s/ consistently.

selections.sense: provide grounds that establish a claim or relation

selections.levelRationale: Allows a speaker to narrow a general claim to a particular actionable case.

selections.sense: necessary in such a way that the intended goal cannot be achieved without it

selections.sense: affecting or including only part of the relevant whole
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes limited coverage or agreement from a complete result without treating it as simply a small quantity.

selections.formNotes: Gender-invariant parcial; parciales; resultado/acuerdo parcial; biased judgment is a separate sense.

selections.sense: applying to every member within the relevant domain
selections.levelRationale: Makes the scope of a general claim explicit so exceptions can challenge it.

selections.pronunciationNotes: u-ni-ver-SAL; final stress; v as /b/, final l.

selections.sense: state the distinguishing meaning or limits of a concept
selections.levelRationale: Supports agreeing what a term or category means before evaluating an argument.

selections.sense: present in a small amount relative to what is needed or expected
selections.levelRationale: Allows adequacy-relative shortage to modify a resource directly rather than describe only count size.

selections.sense: present in a relatively large supply
selections.levelRationale: Gives the complementary supply condition without asserting that the amount is excessive or wasteful.

selections.sense: restricted in extent or amount by a specified boundary

selections.sense: not enough for the stated purpose or requirement
selections.levelRationale: Names a failed adequacy condition rather than only a small count, useful for comparing options against a requirement.

selections.sense: at or below a stated upper limit
selections.levelRationale: Expresses an inclusive ceiling, avoiding ambiguity between fewer than and no more than.

selections.sense: at or above a stated lower limit
selections.levelRationale: Expresses an inclusive floor, needed for requirements where exactly the threshold qualifies.

selections.sense: quantity expressed as a number of parts in each hundred

selections.sense: expressed in a base-ten form that may include a fractional part
selections.levelRationale: Supports identifying decimal notation in practical measurement and pricing explanations.

selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Transitive unir and result unirse; regular -ir; social joining may share parent but institutional membership is separately scoped.
selections.pronunciationNotes: u-NIR; final r; no consonant before initial vowel.

selections.sense: attach one surface or object to another so it adheres
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes adhering from loose proximity or general connection in practical object handling.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-W117 pegar pastes digital content; that earlier interface action cannot automatically establish the physical adhesion sense.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Pegar algo a/en otra superficie; pego/pegue; striking someone is separate.
selections.pronunciationNotes: pe-GAR; /g/ preserved by gu in pegue with silent u.
uncertainties: Digital paste is a metaphorical related operation but different selected sense; physical adhesion may deserve earlier H/W introduction, still proposed here.

selections.sense: move someone or something from one location to another
selections.levelRationale: Supports explaining a relocation without encoding the speaker-relative direction of bring or take.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-F068 llevar and069 traer encode direction relative to a reference; B1-F154 mover need not change to a new location.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Transitive trasladar algo/a alguien; trasladarse for moving oneself; translating language is not this verb's selected sense.
selections.pronunciationNotes: tras-la-DAR; sl boundary, final r.
uncertainties: General relocation versus earlier transport verbs may support an earlier introduction; B2 proposal is lexical selection, not proof that taking a new object is a new sense.

selections.sense: move something while it remains in contact with a surface by pulling it
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes dragging from carrying and pushing, relevant to describing a movement mechanism.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-W113 arrastrar is on-screen dragging; the physical contact/pulling operation is related but must be explicitly compared.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Transitive arrastrar; arrastrarse for one's body would need P context; keep result motion rather than figurative emotional influence.
selections.pronunciationNotes: a-rras-TRAR; rr trill and final tr/r sequence.
uncertainties: Physical versus digital drag may be one metaphor-linked parent; don't count as unrelated new word.

selections.sense: move backward or return to an earlier position in a sequence
selections.levelRationale: Provides the opposite of advancing along a path and a clear step-back operation.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-C095 avanzar moves forward; A1-F178 volver returns to a place without specifying backward movement.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Usually intransitive retroceder; retrocedo/retroceda regular -er; abstract retreat follows same directional relation provisionally.
selections.pronunciationNotes: re-tro-ce-DER; initial trill, tr cluster, c /θ/ or /s/.

selections.sense: remaining balanced or resistant to unintended change or movement
selections.levelRationale: Describes persistence or steadiness as a relevant property rather than merely being motionless at one moment.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F155 parar A1 is stop; B1-F150 separado concerns relation, not whether a state is likely to persist.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Gender-invariant estable; estables; physical balance and steady condition provisionally related; exclude clinical assurances.
selections.pronunciationNotes: es-TA-ble; bl cluster.
uncertainties: P may use estable for a reported condition; that does not authorize medical prognosis or a separate guaranteed-stability meaning.

selections.sense: liable to change or lose balance rather than remain steady
selections.levelRationale: Names the opposite risk of fluctuation or unsteadiness without implying that failure has already occurred.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F208 frágil concerns ease of damage; instability concerns persistence/balance, not necessarily fragility.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Gender-invariant inestable; inestables; no automatic derivation of every negative adjective into a separate entry.
selections.pronunciationNotes: i-nes-TA-ble; retain the initial vowel sequence and consonants without adding a vowel into bl.
uncertainties: Bounded productive contrast with estable; physical versus changing-situation scope needs final parent review.

selections.sense: period associated with distinctive circumstances or a stage of life or history
selections.levelRationale: Frames an account by a characteristic period rather than requiring a precise date.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F132 año is a fixed calendar unit; B1-F056 década measures ten years, whereas época has context-defined boundaries.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine época; épocas; en aquella época; no separate era taxonomy required.
selections.pronunciationNotes: É-po-ca; first syllable stress marked.

selections.sense: part of the night after midnight and before ordinary morning activity or dawn
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes the early-night-to-dawn period from tarde, noche and mañana for precise event accounts.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F148 medianoche is a point and A1-F146 noche a broader span; this is the intervening early-hours part.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine madrugada; de madrugada; exact clock boundary is contextual, not a universal fixed timetable.
selections.pronunciationNotes: ma-dru-GA-da; dr cluster; intervocalic d may weaken.

selections.sense: during the initial part of a named period
selections.levelRationale: Places an event within a rough segment without pretending to know its exact date.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F050 al principio is a deictic beginning; the de complement names the relevant month, year or other period.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Fixed plural principios in phrase; de+period; no new row per month/year value.
selections.pronunciationNotes: a prin-CI-pios de; io diphthong; s/de boundary.

selections.sense: during the middle part of a named period
selections.levelRationale: Completes the useful early/middle/late period contrast for approximate timing.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F175 en el centro de is spatial; this expression locates time in a period rather than a physical middle.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Fixed plural mediados; de+time span; not exact mathematical halfway unless context says so.
selections.pronunciationNotes: a me-DIA-dos de; ia diphthong; natural linking of dos/de.

selections.sense: during the closing part of a named period
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes late-in-period timing from an event's eventual outcome.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F006 al final gives a final outcome or point; this phrase identifies the last segment of a named period.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Fixed plural finales; de+period; before the period ends, not necessarily after it.
selections.pronunciationNotes: a fi-NA-les de; ordinary lexical stress and linked phrase.

selections.sense: over a relatively extended future period
selections.levelRationale: Supports comparing a delayed horizon with immediate effects without specifying an arbitrary universal length.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F009 plazo already names a time limit; a long-term horizon is not merely a later deadline.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Invariable phrase; plazo singular; contrast with a corto plazo; timescale must be stated by context.
selections.pronunciationNotes: a LAR-go PLA-zo; pl cluster; z /θ/ or /s/.
uncertainties: Same planned meaning as A2-S191/B1-S218/B1-W190, all B2 proposals; F supplies general temporal parent, not a separate financial sense.

selections.sense: over a relatively near future period
selections.levelRationale: Provides the contrasting horizon needed to weigh immediate against extended consequences.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F152 pronto predicts soon; a corto plazo frames a period of planning rather than promising immediate action.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Fixed phrase; corto does not vary; what counts as short depends on context, not a fixed number of days.
selections.pronunciationNotes: a COR-to PLA-zo; r tap and pl cluster.

selections.sense: having occurred or appeared not long before the reference time
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes recent occurrence from current existence and from a newly acquired object's condition.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F199 nuevo may describe unused/newly acquired; B1-F041 actualmente concerns now, not how long ago an event happened.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Gender-invariant reciente; recientes; reciente relative to a reference time, not an exact day cutoff.
selections.pronunciationNotes: re-CIEN-te; initial trill, ie diphthong; c /θ/ or /s/.

selections.sense: during the interval occupied by another stated event or wait
selections.levelRationale: Connects a parallel activity to an already established interval without needing to repeat its full clause.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F005 mientras introduces a subordinate simultaneous event; this adverbial stands with its own clause and refers back.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Two-word adverbial, not SCONJ merely because it links discourse; punctuation follows clause structure.
selections.pronunciationNotes: MIEN-tras TAN-to; ie diphthong and natural phrase grouping.
uncertainties: Temporal adverb versus connective analysis must be shared with D; do not duplicate while/meanwhile through longer sentences.

selections.sense: occur at the same time or share a matching feature with another event or item
selections.levelRationale: Describes concurrence directly and supports explaining scheduling clashes or matching circumstances.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F034 al mismo tiempo expresses temporal simultaneity; same-batch coincidencia names an unplanned match, while coincidir need not imply accident.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Coincidir con/en; regular -ir; agreement of opinions is a related but separately scoped possible sense.
selections.pronunciationNotes: coincidir stresses final DIR; initial oi grouping can vary, not a mandatory co-in hiatus; c /θ/ or /s/.
uncertainties: Time concurrence versus matching feature may split at global adjudication; this bounded relation is not an agreement claim.

selections.sense: day or immediately preceding period before a named event
selections.levelRationale: Allows timing relative to a reference event rather than only relative to today.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F141 ayer is the day before today; víspera can precede a past or future named event.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine víspera; la víspera de, en vísperas de wider imminent period; not a fixed festival vocabulary list.
selections.pronunciationNotes: VÍS-pe-ra; first stress, medial tap.

selections.sense: after the stated interval has elapsed
selections.levelRationale: Makes elapsed delay from an established reference point explicit.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F035 dentro de looks forward from a reference; al cabo de commonly narrates what follows an elapsed interval, not an exact synonym in every context.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Fixed al cabo de+duration; cabo headword geographical cape is outside scope.
selections.pronunciationNotes: al CA-bo de; b between vowels may approximate; de unstressed.

selections.sense: move a scheduled time or action to an earlier point
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes changing the schedule earlier from merely arriving early or overtaking a vehicle.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F151 temprano describes timing; B1-H126 por adelantado is advance performance, not necessarily rescheduling.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Transitive adelantar una cita/la fecha; adelantarse for an event occurring early is related; traffic passing separate.
selections.pronunciationNotes: a-de-lan-TAR; final r, no written accent.

selections.sense: move or cause an event to occur later than previously expected
selections.levelRationale: Gives the complementary schedule shift without confusing it with cancelling the event.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-T033 retrasarse (planned a2-travel-repair-planned-02) already means running late; B1-T032 aplazar deliberately moves an event later. Retrasar selects causative schedule delay, not a new late-occurrence sense.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Transitive retrasar algo; pronominal retrasarse is an inherited A2 result counterpart, not a newly introduced B2 sense. Regular -ar.
selections.pronunciationNotes: re-tra-SAR; initial strong r and tr cluster.
uncertainties: Compare A2-T033 earlier retrasarse and B1-T032 aplazar; transitive/pronominal parent and B1 versus B2 lexical introduction need adjudication.

selections.sense: point or initial stage at which an activity begins
selections.levelRationale: Makes the start a discussable phase rather than merely using a begin verb.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F244 empezar and B1-F186 comenzar initiate activity; the noun identifies its beginning, not a separate advanced act.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Masculine inicio; inicios; inicio de; inicio of interface/start page in W may share a metaphorical parent.
selections.pronunciationNotes: i-NI-cio; final io diphthong; c /θ/ or /s/.

selections.sense: bring an activity to its endpoint or reach that endpoint
selections.levelRationale: Provides a neutral-to-formal endpoint verb for organized process accounts, without asserting that the endpoint was successful.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F245 terminar and B1-F187 acabar already mean ending; this is a lexical/register alternative, not first completion.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Transitive/intransitive finalizar; finalizo/finalice keeps c/z sound; finalizado regular.
selections.pronunciationNotes: fi-na-li-ZAR; c/z /θ/ or /s/.
uncertainties: Synonym economy with terminar/acabar may favour recognition-only or earlier introduction; no distinct outcome created by register.

selections.sense: stop pursuing or participating in an activity before its intended completion
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes giving up a course of action from finishing it or temporarily pausing.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F013 dejar de marks cessation generally; abandoning adds loss of continued pursuit, not necessarily a successful endpoint.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Abandonar un plan/actividad; regular -ar; leaving a person without care is outside the selected activity sense.
selections.pronunciationNotes: a-ban-do-NAR; final r and four syllables.

selections.sense: extending without a relevant interruption
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes an uninterrupted process from one that happens often but has gaps.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F189 sin parar already describes uninterrupted activity; frequency A1-F154 siempre is not always a measured continuous span.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Continuo/continua adjective; distinguish continúo verb form by stress; continuos/continuas.
selections.pronunciationNotes: con-TI-nuo with usual uo diphthong; not verb con-ti-NÚ-o.

selections.sense: regularly repeated pattern of action acquired or maintained over time
selections.levelRationale: Names an established behavioural pattern for explaining recurrence, not only the number of occasions.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-F107 soler and B1-F038 a menudo express usual/frequent action; hábito is the pattern being discussed.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Masculine hábito; hábitos; tener/adquirir un hábito; religious clothing is outside scope.
selections.pronunciationNotes: HÁ-bi-to; silent h and initial accent.
uncertainties: P/W routine scenarios may justify earlier introduction; adjective habitual is not automatically another entry.

selections.sense: series of stages that can repeat in the same broad order
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes recurring structured sequence from simply doing one action again.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-F105 volver a and B1-F016 express repetition of an action; B1-W141 proceso need not repeat as a cycle.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Masculine ciclo; ciclos; ciclo de; technical biological or engineering cycle types remain with P/W.
selections.pronunciationNotes: CI-clo; cl cluster, initial c /θ/ or /s/.

selections.sense: distinct part of a process characterized by its role or condition
selections.levelRationale: Allows a process to be segmented without assuming that every part has the same length.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-W142 etapa already names a phase of a longer activity; fase is a lexical alternative, not a new stage concept.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine fase; fases; fase de; electrical phase and lunar classification not selected here.
selections.pronunciationNotes: FA-se; two syllables, no accent.
uncertainties: Exact conceptual synonym of earlier etapa may warrant B1 or recognition-only; proposed B2 vocabulary choice remains open.

selections.sense: without a specified boundary or endpoint in the relevant context
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes an unspecified duration from a genuinely infinite duration or a known fixed term.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F009 plazo is a stated limit; indefinido means no bound specified, not necessarily lasting forever.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Indefinido/indefinida; por tiempo indefinido; employment-contract term belongs to W and need not make a separate adjective meaning.
selections.pronunciationNotes: in-de-fi-NI-do; stable unstressed vowels, intervocalic d.

selections.sense: occurring or applying on each day
selections.levelRationale: A compact schedule adjective describes daily recurrence while leaving the action itself inherited.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F158 todos los días already expresses daily recurrence; B1-P176 diario NOUN is a personal record, a different POS/sense.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Diario/diaria; diarios/diarias; no noun newspaper/diary through this row.
selections.pronunciationNotes: DIA-rio; ia and io ordinary diphthongs.
uncertainties: Propose A2 alongside accepted A2-S039 mensual/040 anual; checked general B2 occurrence does not prove daily schedules first begin at B2.

selections.sense: occurring or applying on each week
selections.levelRationale: Completes a practical weekly schedule label alongside inherited monthly/annual labels.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F130 semana names a week and A1-F158 todos los días gives daily recurrence; weekly schedules are not a new B2 communicative function.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Gender-invariant semanal; semanales; a weekly rate or event uses the same periodic relation.
selections.pronunciationNotes: se-ma-NAL; final stress.
uncertainties: Propose A2 with A2-S039 mensual and040 anual, despite B2 general-notion column; lexical introduction is independently judged.

selections.sense: change selected features of something while retaining its general identity
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes partial adjustment from replacing the entire item or turning it into something else.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F280 cambiar replaces one thing with another in its selected sense; B1-F163 organizar arranges rather than necessarily modifies.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Modificar algo; modifico/modifique; no assumption that every edit improves the result.
selections.pronunciationNotes: mo-di-fi-CAR; /k/ maintained in que.

selections.sense: change something substantially into a different form or state
selections.levelRationale: Contrasts substantial transformation with limited modification in explaining a process.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F190 ponerse and191 quedarse express changes of state; transformar foregrounds substantial reworking, not every new adjective context.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Transformar algo en; transformarse en; regular -ar; no promise irreversible transformation.
selections.pronunciationNotes: trans-for-MAR; ns/f boundary and final r.

selections.sense: undergo a change to a new characteristic or state
selections.levelRationale: Supplies a bounded change-of-state construction distinct from returning to a place.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F178 volver is return; B1-F190 ponerse marks a state change already, so differences in durability/control require contextual teaching, not an absolute rule.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Volverse+adjective/noun; vuelvo/vuelva, vuelto; often change not presented as deliberate, but avoid categorical permanent/involuntary rules.
selections.pronunciationNotes: vol-VER-se; vuelvo /bwel/; se unstressed.
uncertainties: Ponerse/quedarse/hacerse/volverse form a contextual change-construction system; each is not mechanically limited to one permanent/temporary category.

selections.sense: come to have a new status or characteristic through a developing process
selections.levelRationale: Names gradual or adopted development without confusing making an object with becoming something.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F225 hacer performs a task and A2-F171 produces something; pronominal becoming is different, compared with B1-F190 ponerse.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Hacerse+adjective/noun; hago/haga/hecho; agency and gradualness are tendencies, not mandatory semantic tests.
selections.pronunciationNotes: ha-CER-se; h silent, c /θ/ or /s/; hecho HE-cho.
uncertainties: Status choice belongs partly to P/W; preserve shared construction parent and avoid rigid voluntariness rules.

selections.sense: continue to be in a place or state over an interval
selections.levelRationale: Describes sustained location/state rather than an action continuing or a momentary result.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-F071 quedarse remains in a location; B1-F191 quedarse marks resulting state; permanecer is a persistence-focused lexical alternative.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Permanecer en/+adjective; permanezco/permanezca; neutral-formal register compared with quedarse.
selections.pronunciationNotes: per-ma-ne-CER; /θ/ or /s/; permanezco cluster.
uncertainties: Earlier quedarse may cover the practical persistence concept; proposed B2 lexical register, not a novel state created by longer duration.

selections.sense: with no additional relevant person, thing or condition included
selections.levelRationale: Marks restriction with a neutral-to-formal alternative useful for explicitly limiting a claim.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-F178 solo already means only; a longer explanation does not create a new exclusive relation.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Invariable -mente adverb; keep written accent from única; avoid a second row for only just as a time reading.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Ú-ni-ca-MEN-te; retains adjective and -mente stress sites.
uncertainties: Same basic exclusion as A2-F178 solo; synonym economy and introduction should be adjudicated rather than treating it as conceptually new.

selections.sense: boundary beyond which the relevant extent, amount or permission does not continue
selections.levelRationale: A boundary noun connects spatial and quantitative constraints without assuming a numerical threshold is always exceeded.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-F049/050 threshold comparisons and B1-F196 lado do not name the boundary itself.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Masculine límite; límites; límite de/entre; legal enforcement is not implied by the word.
selections.pronunciationNotes: LÍ-mi-te; written accent on first syllable.
uncertainties: Spatial boundary and abstract amount cap are provisionally a common relation; final granularity review should not create one sense per domain.

selections.sense: bending continuously rather than forming a straight line or flat direction
selections.levelRationale: Describes a shaped object's bend rather than a road feature alone.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-T044 curva is a bend in a route; B1-F193–202 shapes and orientations leave the straight/curved property contrast explicit.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Curvo/curva; curvos/curvas; noun road bend and this adjective remain POS-distinct.
selections.pronunciationNotes: CUR-vo; medial r and v /b/.

selections.sense: not conforming to a consistent pattern, shape or arrangement
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes uneven/nonuniform form from a merely unusual but regular shape.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F203 plano and211 liso concern flat/even surfaces; irregular can describe inconsistent outline or spacing.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Gender-invariant irregular; irregulares; no silent extension to unlawful conduct or a grammatical paradigm.
selections.pronunciationNotes: i-rre-gu-LAR; rr trill; g is /g/ before pronounced u.

selections.sense: bend or fold an object so that its form changes direction or one part lies over another
selections.levelRationale: Explains changing a shape rather than simply moving the whole object or making two copies.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-C054 doblado is translated voice replacement; same-batch duplicar multiplies amount, not physical folding.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Doblar algo; doblarse for result; regular -ar; doubling a quantity and dubbing are different selected senses.
selections.pronunciationNotes: do-BLAR; bl cluster and final r.

selections.sense: resisting bending or deformation rather than yielding flexibly
selections.levelRationale: Complements flexible materials when explaining suitability or movement limits.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F209 flexible bends without breaking; B1-F206 duro concerns resistance to pressure, which is not identical to rigidity.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Rígido/rígida; plurals; figurative inflexibility in rules needs contextual adjudication, not automatic new sense.
selections.pronunciationNotes: RÍ-gi-do; g before i /x/ or regional variant; written accent.

selections.sense: able to stretch or deform and then recover its previous shape
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes recoverable stretching from simple bending or softness.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F209 flexible can bend but need not recover its exact shape; B1-F207 blando yields to pressure without elastic recovery.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Elástico/elástica; plurals; adjective material property, not a separately selected elastic band noun.
selections.pronunciationNotes: e-LÁS-ti-co; written accent, st cluster.

selections.sense: stretched or drawn tight rather than loose
selections.levelRationale: Names a mechanical state relevant to cords or fabric without inferring emotional distress.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F206 duro is hardness; a soft rope can be tense, so this is not merely a stronger hard adjective.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Tenso/tensa; tensos/tensas; emotional tensión context is not selected by the physical gloss.
selections.pronunciationNotes: TEN-so; ns boundary.

selections.sense: not held, stretched or fastened firmly enough in the relevant context
selections.levelRationale: Supplies the loose counterpart for explaining adjustment or a fault.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-P088 débil is little bodily strength; B1-H faults do not automatically name looseness of a fastening.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Flojo/floja; plurals; lax effort or low intensity are other possible senses, not selected.
selections.pronunciationNotes: FLO-jo; fl cluster, j /x/ or regional weaker sound.

selections.sense: having a thick consistency that makes a liquid flow less readily
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes consistency from the quantity or temperature of a liquid.

selections.sense: wet throughout with a large amount of absorbed liquid

selections.sense: gaseous form produced from a substance normally encountered as a liquid

selections.sense: combination of components brought together in one material or preparation
selections.levelRationale: Supports discussing composition without requiring that the components chemically react or become indistinguishable.

selections.sense: powdered binding material used in building mixtures that harden

selections.sense: manufactured block commonly used to build walls
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes a countable building unit from loose binder or raw stone.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-S090 piedra is a piece of rock; a manufactured wall block has a distinct ordinary use and form.

selections.sense: reddish metallic material used in items such as wiring and pipes
selections.levelRationale: Provides one bounded material contrast for explaining familiar components rather than listing all chemical elements.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F217 acero/218 hierro are earlier metals; cobre differs materially, not a new general metal concept.

selections.sense: synthetic fibre or material used especially in textiles

selections.sense: allowing objects behind it to be seen through it
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes visibility through a material from that material merely being pale or well lit.

selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Gender-invariant transparente; transparentes; openness of an institution is a different possible metaphor.
selections.pronunciationNotes: trans-pa-REN-te; initial ns/p boundary.

selections.sense: preventing light from passing through the material
selections.levelRationale: Supplies the opposite permeability-to-sight property without equating it with dark colour.

uncertainties: Original complementary selection; exact opaco occurrence not asserted from the checked B1/B2 examples.

selections.sense: recognize a perceptual difference or identify something among similar stimuli
selections.levelRationale: Adds discrimination between similar items rather than mere perception of one stimulus.

selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Distinguir algo de/entre; distingo/distinga, distinguir with silent u after g; honouring a person is outside scope.
selections.pronunciationNotes: dis-tin-GUIR; gu before i gives hard /g/ with silent u; distingo /g/.

selections.sense: sound heard again after reflection from a surface
selections.levelRationale: Supports explaining a repeated sound without confusing it with a second deliberate speaker.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F228 sonido is sound generally; B1-F231 sonar emits/resounds but does not name this reflected repetition.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.

selections.pronunciationNotes: E-co; two syllables, /k/.

selections.sense: pitch height or pitch quality of a sound or voice
selections.levelRationale: Separates how high/low a sound is from how loud it is played.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-C140 volumen is loudness and B1-F230 voz a voice; pitch is a different auditory dimension.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.

selections.sense: high in pitch when describing a sound
selections.levelRationale: Provides the high-pitch member of an audible contrast rather than a loudness judgment.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F183 alto is height and B1-C140 volumen loudness; neither safely conveys pitch without this specific scope.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Agudo/aguda; sonido/voz agudo/a; acute pain, sharp point and cleverness not selected.
selections.pronunciationNotes: a-GU-do; g before u ordinary /g/.

selections.sense: low in pitch when describing a sound
selections.levelRationale: Provides the low-pitch counterpart without implying a serious problem.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: No exact grave/gravedad earlier row was found in the inspected A1/A2/B1 index; A1-P039 serio means serious rather than joking and A2-P067 urgente requires prompt attention, neither is low sound pitch.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Grave gender-invariant; graves; tono/voz grave; no automatic health-severity meaning.
selections.pronunciationNotes: GRA-ve; gr cluster, v /b/.

selections.sense: having little or no perceptible flavour
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes weak taste from an unpleasant or bitter taste in material/food descriptions.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-H029 soso is insufficient seasoning/flavour for the speaker; insípido foregrounds near-absence of flavour, with possible synonym overlap.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Insípido/insípida; plurals; figurative dullness not selected.
selections.pronunciationNotes: in-SÍ-pi-do; accent on sí, intervocalic d.
uncertainties: Exact overlap with B1-H029 soso may support earlier introduction or a single underlying blandness sense; H owns food preference context.

selections.sense: distinctive smell, commonly perceived or presented as pleasant
selections.levelRationale: Supplies a positive or characteristic smell description without treating all smells as pleasant.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F238 olor and B1-P052/B1-H046 give neutral smell; aroma adds conventional evaluative/characteristic framing.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Masculine el aroma despite final -a; aromas; aroma de; no claim aroma proves safety or taste quality.
selections.pronunciationNotes: a-RO-ma; medial tap.

selections.sense: having the colour or appearance of gold without necessarily being made of gold
selections.levelRationale: Separates surface colour from material composition when describing or comparing objects.

selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.

selections.pronunciationNotes: do-RA-do; intervocalic d may weaken.

selections.sense: having the colour or appearance of silver without necessarily being made of silver
selections.levelRationale: Completes the useful metallic-colour versus metal-material distinction.

selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.

selections.pronunciationNotes: pla-te-A-do; e-a hiatus; pl cluster.

selections.sense: having a surface that does not reflect light with a glossy shine
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes finish from colour and transparency when comparing surfaces.

selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.

selections.pronunciationNotes: MA-te; two syllables, no accent.

selections.sense: make something dirty or leave unwanted soiling on it
selections.levelRationale: Names causing loss of cleanliness rather than the resulting dirt or a stain alone.

selections.sense: extent to which people with relevant needs can reach and use a place, service or information

selections.sense: dependent on a person's perspective or judgment rather than only shared observable criteria

selections.sense: inconsistent with reason or the relevant premises to an implausible degree

selections.sense: of a very high standard in the relevant respect
selections.levelRationale: A high-quality judgment can be qualified by criteria, without accumulating every praise synonym.

selections.sense: providing sufficient financial return relative to its costs

selections.sense: well suited to the purpose, situation or audience concerned

selections.sense: change one's behaviour or functioning to fit new conditions

uncertainties: Original complementary selection under precision scenario; exact source example occurrence not asserted.

selections.sense: reason or drive that prompts someone to undertake or continue an activity

selections.sense: having the ability or capacity needed to perform the specified action

selections.sense: judgment reached after considering the preceding information or reasoning

selections.formNotes: El que/la que/los que/las que; preposition as required; neuter lo que refers to an unexpressed thing/proposition, treated as paradigm-related grammar rather than every form a new word.
selections.pronunciationNotes: el que and forms normally unstressed as relative units; distinguish interrogative qué by accent/prosody.
uncertainties: Relative-pronoun unit versus article plus relative analysis and lo que granularity remain global grammar/identity decisions; all agreement variants are not net-new lexical senses.

selections.sense: mark a change affecting the subject without presenting an external agent as performing it
selections.levelRationale: Separates a middle change of state from literal self-action, reciprocal action and passive presentation.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Earlier bounded middle forms already include A2-H014 estropearse, A2-H152 romperse, B1-S155 secarse and B1-W155 evaporarse; unlike A2-P070 reflexive self-drying. B2 extends productive analysis, not first availability of these words.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Middle se with a changing subject; verb agrees with affected subject; not all intransitive changes require se; no implication the subject intentionally acted on itself.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Unstressed se linked to the verb; agreement endings need intelligibility.
uncertainties: Likely grammar metadata within one se family, not a new globally unique word; preserve the distinct analysis if lexical rows merge.
Earlier bounded change-of-state senses remain at their proposed levels; full productive middle analysis is not inferred from one earlier form or deferred wholesale to B2.

selections.sense: combine with an affected-person dative to frame an event as happening to someone rather than deliberate agency
selections.levelRationale: Explains the accidental/affected-person construction in reports without claiming it proves absence of responsibility.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F170 impersonal omits an actor and171 passive highlights affected subject; se me/te/le additionally identifies an affected person.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Se+me/te/le/nos/os/les before finite verb; se precedes dative, then verb agrees with affected subject; not a pronoun variant fixed to me.
selections.pronunciationNotes: Clitics unstressed and linked; keep se+dative order audible, no inserted emphasis.
uncertainties: PCIC grammar7.1.4 treats this as responsibility-mitigating framing; it does not establish factual blamelessness. Construction-versus-lexical-row policy remains open.

selections.sense: not existing in the relevant place, time or domain
selections.levelRationale: Names the absence of existence as a property without confusing it with an existing thing being hidden or missing.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F061 existir supplies existence and F063 desaparecer ceased presence; nonexistent is not necessarily previously present.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Gender-invariant inexistente; inexistentes; scope must be specified rather than an unsupported universal denial.
selections.pronunciationNotes: i-ne-xis-TEN-te; x usually /ks/; no extra syllable in cluster.

selections.sense: not open to view or readily accessible to observation
selections.levelRationale: Separates something being hidden from not existing at all.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F226 invisible cannot be seen in context; hidden can be deliberately concealed but that intention is not required.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Oculto/oculta; plurals; oculto a/tras; no automatic covert-intent claim.
selections.pronunciationNotes: o-CUL-to; lt boundary.

selections.sense: put something where it is not readily found or seen
selections.levelRationale: Names the concealment action rather than the resulting hidden state.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F065 perder A2 mislays unintentionally; esconder ordinarily involves deliberate concealment, not every lost item.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Transitive esconder; esconderse for hiding oneself; regular -er; no concealment advice for evading rules.
selections.pronunciationNotes: es-con-DER; nd cluster, final r.

selections.sense: part of a whole that remains after another part is removed or considered
selections.levelRationale: Supports explaining the remaining allocation rather than merely a surplus beyond need.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B2-F013 sobrar is excess beyond need; a remainder may still be required or insufficient.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Masculine resto; el resto de; restos remains/debris may be related but not automatically selected.
selections.pronunciationNotes: RES-to; initial trill and st boundary.

selections.sense: divisible into two equal whole-number groups with no remainder, of an integer
selections.levelRationale: Adds the bounded even/odd classification needed for numeric ordering and simple explanations.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1 number forms name values; B1-F128 dividir supplies division but does not label this integer property.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Gender-invariant par; pares; números pares; pair noun is separate, not equivalent to every quantity of two.
selections.pronunciationNotes: PAR; single syllable, final r.

selections.sense: not divisible into two equal whole-number groups without a remainder, of an integer
selections.levelRationale: Provides the complementary integer classification without selecting an unlimited set of individual numbers.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A1-F090 cuarto is ordinal position; odd integer is neither third nor an unusual quality.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Gender-invariant impar; impares; integer scope only.
selections.pronunciationNotes: im-PAR; final stress and r.

selections.sense: metric length unit equal to one thousandth of a metre
selections.levelRationale: Names a small linear unit used in practical dimensions without introducing an entire specialist measurement taxonomy.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-F129 centímetro is one hundredth of a metre; millimetre is a different scale, not the area or volume of an object.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Masculine milímetro; milímetros; symbol mm does not take plural -s; number/unit formatting belongs to W conventions.
selections.pronunciationNotes: mi-LÍ-me-tro; accent on lí; tr cluster.

selections.sense: metric mass unit equal to one thousand kilograms
selections.levelRationale: Adds a large mass scale for comparing loads or resource quantities rather than only household measures.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: Earlier kilo/gramo weight quantities are inherited H/W; tonelada scales mass, not a volume or arbitrary large-number metaphor.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine tonelada; toneladas; tonne symbol t; do not confuse differing nonmetric tons when translating.
selections.pronunciationNotes: to-ne-LA-da; intervocalic d can weaken.

selections.sense: distance from an opening, surface or boundary inward or downward
selections.levelRationale: Lets an explanation compare depth independently of height or surface area.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F137 profundo is the depth property; the noun names the measured dimension.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine profundidad; profundidades; profundidad de; figurative intellectual depth outside selected physical scope.
selections.pronunciationNotes: pro-fun-di-DAD; pr cluster and final d.

selections.sense: place or source from which a person, thing or material comes
selections.levelRationale: Names source origin as a relation rather than destination or ownership.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F160 origen retained A1 already gives origin; procedencia is a neutral-formal source label, not first origin communication.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Feminine procedencia; procedencias; procedencia de; no inference of identity/beliefs from origin.
selections.pronunciationNotes: pro-ce-DEN-cia; c /θ/ or /s/, final ia diphthong.
uncertainties: Earlier origen may support earlier introduction or recognition-only synonym; not a new concept because the source is a material.

selections.sense: one of the possible directions of movement along a route or axis
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes opposite directions on the same route from the route itself.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-D125 sentido is intended meaning of a statement; B1-F159 dirección gives direction broadly, so overlap is explicit.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Masculine sentido; sentidos; en sentido contrario, sentido de marcha; sensory faculty and semantic meaning separate.
selections.pronunciationNotes: sen-TI-do; intervocalic d may weaken.
uncertainties: Directional sentido and earlier dirección require shared granularity review; no new route sense just because instructions are longer.

selections.sense: have spent the stated interval without performing an action or experiencing an event
selections.levelRationale: Tracks a continuing absence of activity, not the duration of an activity that is occurring.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F185 llevar+gerund tracks continued doing; A2-F097 todavía no signals not yet without specifying elapsed absence.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Llevar+duration+sin+infinitive; llevo regular; duration obligatory to selected pattern; no fixed sentence entries.
selections.pronunciationNotes: lle-VAR sin; sin unstressed, final r/s linking.
uncertainties: Construction metadata may share llevar duration parent; productive absence pattern is preserved even if lexical rows merge.

selections.sense: continue not to perform an action or not to have a stated condition
selections.levelRationale: Distinguishes persistence of nonoccurrence from stopping an action that was happening.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: A2-F106 seguir+gerund continues doing; B1-F013 dejar de stops doing, whereas seguir sin can continue an absence from the start.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: Seguir sin+infinitive; sigo/siga, siguiendo; no mandatory duration phrase unlike llevar sin.
selections.pronunciationNotes: se-GUIR sin; gu silent u before i, hard g; siguiendo /gje/.

selections.sense: continue or repeatedly perform an activity despite a negated cessation expression
selections.levelRationale: Captures the conventional persistence reading where literal stopping would reverse the intended meaning.
selections.lowerLevelContrast: B1-F013 dejar de means cease; negating it can mark continued doing, not a new lexical verb for each activity.
selections.region: Pan-Hispanic; es-ES audio target without treating other varieties as errors.
selections.formNotes: No dejar de+infinitive; negation scope matters; ordinary literal 'not stop' and emphatic frequency readings must be context-scoped.
selections.pronunciationNotes: no de-JAR de; j /x/ or regional variant; both de syllables remain clear.
uncertainties: May remain a construction/use note under dejar de instead of a globally unique lexical entry; no artificial count for transparent negated sentences.
